messages:
jia: quick heads-up — after yesterday's canary (mixtral-16b, rope-scaling=1.07, kernel-scheduler=v2) we saw a ~15% p95 tail latency uplift and a small but consistent jitter spike across regions. opening thread to triage.

matt: do we have a flamegraph / perf profile yet? any obvious hotspot (memcpy, dtype-conversion, scheduler churn)?

sara: posting a short perf sample from the canary box (host: canary-7):\n\n```
# perf top snapshot (aggregated)
  32.5%  runtime_kernel_dispatch
  18.0%  kv_cache_eviction_walk
  11.2%  dtype_cast_fp8_to_fp16
   9.3%  batch_scheduler::select_kernel_robin
   6.1%  align_memcpy_16b
```

Observation: scheduler is flipping between an fp16 kernel and our fp8-fast path on a per-batch basis. the dtype cast shows up non-trivial. also kv eviction walk climbs when prefix-cache warmups happen (long docs). :thinking: 

ryan: hm — that kernel flip is interesting. saw similar in lab when batch sizes hovered near the kernel-robin threshold. the scheduler chooses kernel by (batch_size, seq_len, detected_fp8_safe). with rope-scaling bumped, effective head interactions change token churn which nudges typical batch_len distribution. proposal: increase the kernel-robin hysteresis and add a sticky kernel selection per-stream for 2s to avoid flip-flopping.

perf-bot: deploy.bot noticed canary deploy 2026-03-17T02:15:00Z -> mixtral-16b:v23.4-rollout in production (50%).

jia: thanks. to reproduce locally:\n\n```
# reproduce one-off micro-run
./run_infer --model mixtral-16b --rope-scale 1.07 --kernel-scheduler v2 \
  --batch-policy adaptive --min-batch 4 --max-batch 32 --kv-precision fp8

# collect perf
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- ./run_infer ... && sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > f.svg
```

matt: quick A/B microbench (same region) numbers from the canary window:\n\n```
config A (baseline, kernel-scheduler=v1, kv-precision=fp16): p50=18ms p95=72ms p99=135ms
config B (canary, kernel-scheduler=v2, kv-precision=fp8): p50=20ms p95=83ms p99=160ms
```

difference mostly at p95/p99. throughput (tokens/s) slightly up for B but tail is worse.

sara: digging deeper — kv_cache_eviction_walk increases CPU with fp8 because our eviction comparator triggers a full key-sweep when quantized size estimation misses alignment (we store quantized sizes in a compressed header). hypothesis: mis-estimate → extra mem touches → cache line churn → scheduler flips due to jitter.

ryan: actionable steps I can run overnight:\n- increase kernel-robin hysteresis from 0.15 -> 0.35 (makes scheduler prefer current kernel until bigger delta)\n- set sticky_kernel_ttl=2000ms for stream level\n- try hybrid kv store: index in fp16 metadata, values quantized fp8 but keep small hot-prefixes in fp16 for alignment-sensitive heads\n\nwill run 6hr microbench across 3 regions and post results.

jia: good. also add a test run disabling fp8-kv (force fp16-kv) to validate hypothesis about eviction_walk correlation. if that fixes tails we can be confident. add logs for eviction count and failed-estimate rate.

perf-bot: perf-suite scheduled: nightly_perf/kv-robin-hysteresis/1893456890 -> run queued (6h).

matt: one more thought — RoPE scaling changes effective attention distribution. that can increase longest-lived kv entries (long documents) causing heavier prefix-cache pressure. suggest an eviction soft-limit: keep prefix-cache entries pinned for 3 seconds after creation if they are reaccessed >2 times. avoids thrash on streaming docs.

sara: noted. I'll add instrumentation: evictions_per_stream, avg_kv_entry_ttl, failed_size_estimate_rate. also will dump kernel selection trace per-batch for 1% of requests so we can correlate flip events to specific seq_len patterns.

jia: plan looks solid. owners: ryan (scheduler patch + microbench), sara (kv instrumentation + trace), matt (analysis + rollback playbook). target: results in morning (12h). if tails persist we rollback v23.4 rollout to 0% and pin to v23.3.

ryan: starting jobs now. will post a summary once complete. :white_check_mark:

sara: pushing instrumentation patch to canary branch, small crash guard added. will watch overnight logs and flag any increase in CPU.

matt: thanks — appreciate quick turnaround.\n\njia: thanks team. will follow up after perf results.
